note: BACK-FILLED 2026-08-03 after the run, from the branch's commit messages, which are the contemporaneous record. Recorded as a Gate 6 finding against this run (CO-7): the ledger should have been created at Step 0 and appended per pass. Two consequences a reviewer must weigh. (1) Rows are reconstructed, not captured live, so a finding raised and silently dropped without reaching a commit message would not appear here - absence is weaker evidence in this fragment than in one written live. (2) The six passes ran with a two-dot 'origin/dev..HEAD' range in the agent prompts while the branch was 5 commits behind dev, so dev-ahead work rendered to the agents as removals; two agents caught it, earlier ones may have been misled. The branch has since been rebased onto b061cd74, so the range above is the corrected three-dot form and no longer reproduces what those agents saw.

summary: The upgrade note said the recall 'refuses a ticket minted by any other surface'. kUnspecified is exempt and every pre-upgrade row decodes to it, so a carried-across REST-minted ticket stays redeemable. The changelog fragment disclosed this; the note did not.

trigger: comment asserts a build guarantee that does not exist
summary: Two comments claimed a new enumerator would fail the build at the security gate. meson.build sets werror=false project-wide, so it warned and exited 0; on MSVC at /W3 the diagnostic is level 4 and silent. The assurance also pointed at the predicate, which fails CLOSED - the site that fails OPEN is to_string. Made true rather than softened.

trigger: the documented way to close the exemption window does not work
summary: The note said to 'reject any outstanding pending or approved tickets'. set_review_status refuses a non-pending row, so an approved ticket cannot be rejected at all, and the redeemable population is exactly approved AND consumed_at = 0. The remedy touched only the harmless rows.

summary: Line 48 said migration v5 back-fills pre-existing rows while line 70, added in the same fold, said it deliberately does NOT. Third round in a row this same fact was wrong. A pre-v5 row reads as '' because the column is added with DEFAULT '' and SQLite does not rewrite existing rows.

trigger: project-wide -Werror=switch / /we4062 is too broad a vehicle
summary: The comment's claim needed to become true; the whole project did not need to change to do it. On MSVC /we outranks /external:W0, so /we4062 would also apply inside vcpkg headers for any inline or template function instantiated from a Yuzu TU. Replaced with file-local pragma regions around exactly the three named switches. Verified in an isolated copy.

trigger: LIMIT 64 rationale had the ordering backwards
summary: The comment said kMcpSubmitterPendingCap is checked before find_pending is reached; find_pending is called at mcp_server.cpp:3150 and the cap check is at :3168 - after, and only on the nullopt path. Third time this same comment stated the mechanism wrongly. It now names the uncoupled invariant underneath: LIMIT must stay greater than the cap, and nothing ties the two numbers.

trigger: mutation verification of the guard
summary: Delete the guard -> 3 red; weaken to refuse-all -> 13 red including both positive controls. All six Gate 8 mutations red, including the fail-open one. Not false-green.

trigger: submit()'s origin defaulted to the exempt value
summary: The default was kUnspecified, the one value the redemption guard exempts. A new mint surface that forgot the argument would produce a whole population of redeemable tickets with no compile error, no failing test and no log line - not hypothetical, the MCP gate reached the 3-argument shape by exactly that route. Default removed; every caller states its surface. Removing it immediately found three unenumerated mint sites in test_mcp_server.cpp.

trigger: a store error tells the caller its live approval is spent
summary: kStoreError returned the constant 'not consumable' message, instructing a client to discard a live human-approved ticket on what is usually a transient SQLITE_BUSY. The header argued this could not be fixed without reopening the oracle; that argument does not hold for kStoreError, which is decided before any id-specific determination. Now a retryable kInternalError.

trigger: pending cap checked before the only expiry sweep in the tree
summary: A queue reaching 1000 pending returned early forever: nothing aged out, the count never fell, and the REST gate, every gated schedule occurrence and every MCP mint were permanently denied - recoverable only by reviewing up to 1000 tickets by hand. The one event that would drain the queue was the one event the cap forbade. Sweep now runs first, with a positive control pinning that a genuinely fresh queue is still refused.

trigger: the forgery refusal moved no metric
summary: Every sibling denial on the same handler calls count_denial; the one case the control exists to stop did not, leaving the operator tailing logs. Now counts yuzu_mcp_approval_denied_total with a fixed reason label, never caller-derived.

trigger: the published remediation statement destroys live MCP approvals
summary: The published UPDATE was scoped to origin='' and described as 'the exempt population, and only that'. That is true, and it is why it was dangerous: the MCP mint also records origin='', so the statement revoked every live MCP ticket. Run periodically - the natural reading of 'close the window' - it livelocks MCP approvals outright. Now bounded by submitted_at against a captured epoch, with the bound's reason stated at the command.
